AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: An association between congenital heart disease (CHD) and infantile cholestasis, a key finding for the diagnosis of biliary atresia (BA), remains unknown. The aim of this study was to investigate the characteristics of direct hyperbilirubinemia (D-HB) in infants with CHD.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: All neonates who were admitted to our hospital and diagnosed with CHD in 2015 and 2016 were included. D-HB (direct bilirubin≧ 2.0 mg/dL) within 60 days of age and other clinical parameters were retrospectively reviewed. Statistical analysis between patients with/without D-HB was performed by chi square test or Wilcoxon rank sum test.

AbstractText.Label: RESULT
AbstractText.content: Seventy-six patients (M:F=36:40) were included in this study. Major CHDs were ventricular septal defects in 17, patent ductus arteriosus in 10, and others in 49. Thirteen patients (17.1%) experienced D-HB within 60 days of age. Decrease of D-HB (DB < 2.0 mg/dL) occurred in 10 of the 13 patients during their clinical course at our hospital, which was resolved within seven days in 8 of the 10 patients. Sex, gestational age, birth weight, chromosomal anomalies, need for Fontan operation for CHD repair, and/or cardiac operation were not associated with D-HB within 60 days of age.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: While D-HB was frequently obsereved in infants with CHDs, the majority of D-HB was resolved spontaneously within 1 week. Neonatal clinical parameters or condition of CHD was not predictive of D-HB. D-HB lasting more than 1 week in infants with CHD should be evaluated for the cause.
